headline: Sensex crashes over 900 points and Nifty slips below 22,300 amid hawkish Fed signals and global sell-off

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Hawkish US Fed stance leading to the first foreign outflows from emerging markets since June
Weak global cues including sliding China stocks and rising Treasury yields
Impact of the recent RBI interest rate hike on domestic market sentiment
Rising Brent crude oil prices which increased by 2% during the trading session
whatHappening: Sensex tumbled over 900 points while Nifty 50 dropped below the 22,300 level
IT stocks including TCS and Infosys gained up to 3% despite the broader market crash
Jefferies cut target prices for BSE and other stocks ahead of the Q2 earnings season
Emerging markets are experiencing significant foreign capital outflows as global investors turn cautious
summary: The Indian stock market experienced a major crash on October 8, with the Sensex falling over 900 points due to hawkish Fed commentary and foreign fund outflows. While most sectors faced heavy selling pressure, IT stocks like TCS and Infosys managed to trade higher ahead of their Q2 results. Investors remain cautious as global tech valuations face earnings tests and domestic interest rates remain high.
